meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-04 | Time: 09:00 PT | Duration: 45 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Ortiz, Sofia Alvarez (Redwood) — Priya Patel, Marcus Lee, Dr. Elena Ruiz, Jon Kim (Novum Health)
summary: Intro discovery on Novum's security and hosting requirements. Primary concerns: SOC2 and ISO readiness, SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning, strict RBAC and audit log retention for regulatory review, and KMS integration for envelope encryption. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted (fast onboarding) vs Dedicated (predictable capacity) vs Private/VPC (data residency). Agreed next steps to exchange artifacts and schedule sizing pilot.
topics: Audit logs: retention, schema, and export
Encryption & KMS: CMEK vs Redwood-managed keys
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Daniel and Sofia from our infra SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya Patel: Good morning, thanks. Appreciate it. We're hoping to run through high level security posture and then dig into hosting options — especially KMS and audit logs.
[00:16] Daniel Ortiz: Awesome. Maybe quick round robin on goals — Priya?
[00:20] Priya Patel: Sure. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs a private VPC because we're a healthcare data platform. SOC2 is table stakes, ISO 27001 would be nice to know where Redwood aligns. We also need SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning, and strong RBAC so access maps to our teams.
[00:36] Marcus Lee: And audit logs — for compliance audits we need append-only logs with exportable feeds and retention control. Also envelope encryption with our KMS is a non-negotiable for some data flows.
[00:46] Maya Chen: Totally makes sense. Quick note — Redwood's hosted product is SOC2 Type II and we can share the report redacted; Private deployments let you bring your own KMS, Dedicated gives isolation without full private control. We'll walk the differences.
[00:58] Dr. Elena Ruiz: When you say "bring your own KMS" — do you support Cloud KMS integrations (GCP/AWS/Azure)? Or HSM direct?
[01:06] Sofia Alvarez: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault for CMEK in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we offer an envelope encryption option where you can rotate keys via a customer-managed KMS in a VPC peered flow; HSM direct connections require Private on-prem or a dedicated HSM arrangement.
[01:26] Jon Kim: What's the difference in audit log fidelity between hosted and private? We need full per-request metadata including model, prompt hash, token counts, user id and decision trace.
[01:36] Daniel Ortiz: Currently, our logging schema captures request id, timestamp, model id, route, input size, output token count, response latency, and user-provided identifiers if sent. For Dedicated and Private you can also stream raw audit logs to your S3/GCS/Azure container with full payload if you configure it — subject to PII controls. Hosted retains aggregated logs by default but we can set up per-account exports for enterprise tiers.
[02:01] Priya Patel: Aggregated logs won't pass our auditors. They want event-level records for a rolling 7-year retention in some cases.
[02:08] Maya Chen: Seven years is long — we can support export to your storage and you can set retention as needed. We'll need to scope transfer, egress costs and encryption at rest in the target store.
[02:20] Marcus Lee: On encryption, we need assurance that plaintext never persists on Redwood-managed storage unencrypted. Also, key rotation policies and key access audit details.
[02:29] Sofia Alvarez: For Private and Dedicated, plaintext is not persisted. For Hosted, we use envelope encryption with keys in KMS and layered AES keys internally; all at-rest is encrypted. Key rotation is supported, and we log KMS usage for key access events. We can also provide KMS access logs as part of the audit bundle.
[02:47] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Certification-wise — you said SOC2 Type II. What about ISO 27001 or FedRAMP? Any gap assessments?
[02:55] Maya Chen: We're SOC2 Type II audited; for ISO we have mapped controls and an ISO readiness packet that describes how our controls align with ISO 27001. FedRAMP is not in our current scope. We can share our control mapping and a short gap analysis.
[03:10] Priya Patel: Great. On SSO — SAML is required, SCIM for automated provisioning preferred. Also we need role-mapping to our internal groups.
[03:19] Daniel Ortiz: We integrate with SAML 2.0 and support SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. RBAC is role-based plus attribute-based rules; for Dedicated/Private you can sync groups via SCIM and enforce more granular roles (e.g., read-only auditor, model-deploy, billing-admin). For Hosted there's still RBAC but some enterprise-only roles are gated.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: Can we get an example RBAC matrix? We want to see least-privilege roles and what API scopes each maps to.
[03:47] Maya Chen: Yes — Daniel will add an example matrix to the follow-up packet.
[03:51] Jon Kim: Network restrictions — if we do Dedicated, can we restrict egress to just our VPCs? We want private peering and strong egress controls.
[03:59] Sofia Alvarez: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private deployments you own the VPC entirely. Hosted uses customer-specific tenancy but not VPC-level peering by default; we provide IP allow lists and private link in some regions.
[04:14] Priya Patel: Okay. Let's talk latency/cost tradeoffs quickly. Some of our flows are real-time triage so they'd need p50 < 100ms — can Redwood meet that on Hosted?
[04:23] Daniel Ortiz: On hosted, p50 numbers depend on model family and prompt length. For smaller models and short prompts we've seen p50s in low double-digit milliseconds. For dedicated pools you can get more consistent tail latency. Private on-prem can be lowest latency but adds ops overhead. We'll propose a sizing and benchmark plan.
[04:41] Priya Patel: Sounds good. What about data retention policies? We need to ensure logs and artifacts containing PII are removed on request and provide records for audits.
[04:50] Maya Chen: We support configurable retention windows for user-supplied content in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has default retention, but enterprise agreements can include custom retention and deletion procedures. We also support subject access request workflows — we can delete customer data on request and provide deletion attestations.
[05:06] Marcus Lee: For the PII handling: can Redwood redact or hash parts of prompts server-side before logging?
[05:12] Sofia Alvarez: We have automatic redaction tooling customers can enable; alternatively you can run a pre-send scrub within your stack or use a private deployment where you control the logging pipeline. Redaction rules can be configured but they are heuristic — so we recommend a combined approach.
[05:30] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Our timeline — pilot in six weeks, production by Q4 if everything looks good. Security sign-off is critical before pilot.
[05:38] Maya Chen: Understood. For pilot scoping we'll need to agree on KPIs — Daniel suggested latency targets, throughput, and audit log completeness.
[05:45] Daniel Ortiz: Right. For the pilot we'd propose spinning up a dedicated pool with a small reserved capacity or a private sandbox depending on the data classification. We'll run a synthetic traffic profile and a real-traffic runbook with your PII redaction turned on.
[06:00] Priya Patel: About cost: what's the delta expected between Hosted and Dedicated for our volume?
[06:05] Daniel Ortiz: Very ballpark: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated has committed monthly commit that reduces per-token unit cost but has a baseline. We'll include a simple TCO workup in the follow-up.
[06:15] Marcus Lee: Any enterprise features around key rotation policies and IAM separation? We need separation of duties between platform ops and devs.
[06:22] Sofia Alvarez: We support fine-grained IAM roles and can enforce separation: auditing, billing, model-deploy permissions. For KMS, customer-provided keys mean Redwood doesn't have access to plaintext without a key unwrap event that is logged and can be restricted.
[06:37] Maya Chen: We should also flag that some of the more advanced compliance features — long-term archived logs, custom retention exports — are part of our enterprise package. We'll make pricing notes.
[06:47] Priya Patel: Ok. Can you walk through what the audit bundle looks like for a SOC2 inquiry?
[06:52] Maya Chen: Briefly: redacted SOC2 Type II report, control descriptions, system architecture diagrams, list of subservice organizations, and sample logs/alerts. We also provide a point-by-point mapping to common regulators. We'll send the redacted report and control mapping.
[07:07] Marcus Lee: If we go Private, what's the onboarding time estimate? We're trying to quantify risk vs speed.
[07:13] Daniel Ortiz: Private on-prem typically 8–12 weeks with testing; VPC-hosted Private deployments can be faster if networking is green — more like 4–6 weeks. Dedicated pools usually 2–4 weeks depending on capacity.
[07:26] Dr. Elena Ruiz: For the pilot, we'd likely want dedicated in our cloud region to align with our data residency rules.
[07:32] Maya Chen: Makes sense. We'll propose a dedicated pool in your preferred region for the pilot.
[07:36] Jon Kim: One more technical: Does Redwood persist KV cache between requests? We use conversation state and want to avoid cache leaks between customers.
[07:44] Sofia Alvarez: KV caches are isolated per session/tenant. In Dedicated and Private the runtime enforces tenant boundaries at the process level. For Hosted we use multi-tenant isolation with strict per-tenant KV namespaces and periodic eviction.
[07:58] Priya Patel: Are you able to provide any benchmarks or perf profiles for models under steady load?
[08:03] Daniel Ortiz: Yes — we'll attach perf profiles and sample benchmarks. For the pilot we'll run the same workloads against a dedicated pool and share p50/p90 numbers and token costs.
[08:13] Maya Chen: Quick recap — action items: we'll send SOC2 and ISO mapping, KMS integration notes, RBAC matrix, dedicated sizing/price sketch, and sample logs. Novum will share retention policy, list of regulated fields, and timeline constraints. Any blockers?
[08:30] Marcus Lee: Only thing is our legal will want to see encryption at rest details and specific SLAs for log availability.
[08:36] Maya Chen: We'll include SLA language drafts and log availability guarantees for enterprise contracts.
[08:41] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Sounds good. Let's lock the follow-up call for next week for the sizing deep dive.
[08:46] Maya Chen: I'll send a calendar invite for 60 minutes and include Daniel and Sofia. Thanks everyone.
[08:51] Priya Patel: Thanks very much.
[08:53] (call ends)
